questions.q: Choose the idiom that best replaces the underlined idea: “The project failed due to poor planning.”
questions.why: 'Fell flat' means failed completely. GPSC CBRT, Feb 2026.

questions.q: Identify the figure of speech: “The wind whispered through the trees.”
questions.why: Human action (whispering) given to the wind. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Identify the function of the underlined phrase: “He worked hard in order to succeed.”
questions.why: 'In order to succeed' tells why he worked hard. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to “gregarious”:
questions.why: 'Gregarious' means fond of company; 'reclusive' means avoiding company. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct option: “Hardly had the meeting begun ______ the power failed.”
questions.why: 'Hardly/Scarcely … when'; 'No sooner … than'. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Choose the correct form: “It is no use ____ over spilt milk.”
questions.why: 'It is no use' is followed by a gerund. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to “prudent”:
questions.why: 'Prudent' means careful and sensible; 'reckless' means heedless of danger. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Identify the part of speech of “Neither” in: “Neither of the answers is correct.”
questions.why: It stands for a noun and is followed by 'of'. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct passive construction: “People expect the minister to resign.”
opts: The minister is expected to resign.
It is expected the minister to resign.
questions.why: The same pattern as GPSC's 2026 items: subject + is expected + to-infinitive. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: In the sentence “Wherever you go, I will follow you,” the clause “Wherever you go” is a:
questions.why: 'Wherever' shows place and modifies the verb 'follow'. GPSC-style practice item.
